name: Spaghetti Aglio e Olio
description: A classic Italian pasta dish made with garlic, olive oil, and chilli flakes — simple, bold, and endlessly satisfying. Proof that the best meals need only a handful of great ingredients.
notes: The pasta water is the secret — its starchiness helps emulsify the sauce and makes it cling beautifully to the noodles. Don't skip it! Add it a splash at a time until the sauce is glossy.
steps: Bring a large pot of well-salted water to a boil. Cook spaghetti until al dente. Before draining, reserve 1 cup of starchy pasta water.
While the pasta cooks, peel and thinly slice the garlic cloves. Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-low heat until shimmering.
Add the sliced garlic to the oil and cook gently, stirring often, until golden and fragrant — about 3–4 minutes. Keep the heat low; burnt garlic will ruin the dish.
Add the red chilli flakes and cook for 30 seconds more, letting them bloom in the oil.
Add the drained pasta directly to the skillet with a generous splash of reserved pasta water. Toss vigorously over medium heat.
Remove from heat, add fresh parsley, season generously with salt and black pepper. Serve with grated parmesan if desired.

name: Shakshuka
description: Eggs poached in a rich, spiced tomato and pepper sauce. A one-pan wonder perfect for breakfast, lunch, or dinner.
notes: Make a slight well in the sauce before adding each egg so they stay in place while cooking. Cover the pan to steam the tops of the eggs.
steps: Heat olive oil in a large frying pan over medium heat. Add diced onion and cook for 5 minutes until softened.
Add sliced garlic, cumin, paprika, and chilli flakes. Stir for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in the crushed tomatoes, season with salt and pepper. Simmer for 10 minutes until thickened.
Make 4 wells in the sauce and crack an egg into each. Cover and cook for 5–7 minutes until whites are set but yolks still runny.
Scatter over crumbled feta and fresh parsley. Serve straight from the pan with crusty bread.

name: Chickpea Curry
description: A hearty and fragrant chickpea curry with warming spices and creamy coconut milk. Ready in under 30 minutes and completely vegan.
notes: For a richer curry, let the tomato paste cook for a full 2 minutes before adding the coconut milk — this removes the raw flavour and deepens the sauce.
steps: Heat oil in a large pan over medium heat. Fry the diced onion for 6–8 minutes until golden.
Add garlic, ginger, cumin, coriander, turmeric, and garam masala. Stir for 2 minutes.
Stir in tomato paste and cook for 2 minutes more.
Add drained chickpeas and coconut milk. Stir well, bring to a simmer.
Cook uncovered for 10 minutes until the sauce thickens. Season with salt.
Squeeze in lemon juice, scatter with fresh coriander, and serve with rice or flatbread.

name: Honey Garlic Noodles
description: Silky noodles tossed in a sticky, sweet-savoury honey garlic sauce. On the table in 15 minutes — dangerously addictive.
notes: Don't let the garlic burn — it turns bitter very quickly. Keep the heat medium and stir constantly once it hits the pan.
steps: Cook noodles according to package instructions. Drain and set aside, reserving a splash of cooking water.
Mix together soy sauce, honey, sesame oil, and rice vinegar in a small bowl.
Heat oil in a wok or large frying pan over medium heat. Add minced garlic and cook for 60 seconds.
Pour in the sauce and let it bubble for 30 seconds.
Add the noodles and toss to coat, adding a splash of pasta water to loosen if needed.
Serve topped with sliced spring onions and sesame seeds.

name: Avocado Toast with Poached Eggs
description: A café classic done properly — silky poached eggs on crushed avocado toast with chilli and lemon.
notes: For perfectly poached eggs, add a splash of white wine vinegar to the water before swirling. The acid helps the white hold together.
steps: Bring a pan of water to a gentle simmer. Add a splash of white wine vinegar.
Halve and stone the avocados. Scoop the flesh into a bowl, add lemon juice, salt and pepper, and crush with a fork.
Toast the bread until golden and crisp.
Swirl the simmering water with a spoon, crack in the eggs one at a time, and poach for 3 minutes.
Spread the crushed avocado onto the toast. Top with poached eggs, chilli flakes, and a drizzle of olive oil.
